transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you. Um... well, my wife kind of pushed me to make the appointment. It's just... she'll be telling me things, like about my cousin's appointments or rides he needs, and I'll be looking right at her. But then a minute later, I realize I didn't actually take in half of what she said. So... that's why I'm here.
Do you find that you have this same trouble staying focused or keeping track of details when you are doing other tasks, like work or hobbies?

Yeah, I guess so. Sometimes. Like if I sit down to work out a catering order, or... if I'm listening in on a parish planning call. I'll start off fine. But then... I don't know, my mind just kind of wanders off. I end up having to go back over the same notes, almost like I never even read them in the first place. So... yeah. It happens then, too.
Have you experienced these difficulties with focus and attention since you were a child, or is this a more recent development in your life?

I suppose it's... it's not a new thing. It goes back to when I was a kid. Um... even in grade school, well before I was 12. Teachers used to tell my parents I was bright, but... that I was always daydreaming. I was always leaving my homework in my desk, or needing reminders to just finish my classwork. So... yeah. It's been like this for a long time.
